The deduction is $4,300 (Form 8889 line 13, "the smaller of line 2 or line 12"); the $700 excess is taxed at 6% of the smaller of the excess and the HSAs' value on December 31 ($5,000): $42.00 on Schedule 2 line 8 (f5329 p. 2, line 49). Form 8889 coverage_year completed as changed: the month counts and December 1 coverage are asked and used as recorded, so the recorded values are unchanged.

p590b p. 29, Additional 10% Tax, Example: "Tom Jones, who is 35 years old, receives a $3,000 distribution from his traditional IRA account. Tom doesn't meet any of the exceptions to the 10% additional tax, so the $3,000 is an early distribution. Tom never made any nondeductible contributions to his IRA. ... Tom must also pay an additional tax of $300 (10% (0.10) × $3,000)." The filled-in Form 5329 (p590b p. 32) shows line 1 3000, line 2 -0-, line 3 3000, line 4 300. Class A covers Form 5329 lines 1 to 4 and the $3,000 on Form 1040 line 4b; Schedule 2 line 8 $300 follows from line 4 (f5329 line 4, "Include this amount on Schedule 2 (Form 1040), line 8"). Not asserted: whether Form 5329 is filed and the line 8 box. The example says "He files Form 5329"; the project (D5) takes the no-form path for a code 1 distribution with no exception (i5329 p. 1), so the tax is the same but the form is not prepared. Synthetic scaffolding (not in the example): single, wages $50,000 (the stage18.blind.p1 base with its Marketplace coverage removed, and the Form 1099-R entry of stage10.ira.fully_taxable); Form 1099-R box 7 code 1, the IRA/SEP/SIMPLE box checked, nothing rolled over, no case on the entry screen.

p970 p. 56, chapter 8, Example 1: a teacher (age 32) paid $5,800 of qualified education expenses from $5,000 of tax-free employer-provided educational assistance and an "Early distribution from IRA (taxable part is $500) . . . 3,200"; "Equals: AQEE $ 800"; "Because the teacher’s AQEE ($800) is more than the taxable part of their IRA distribution ($500), they don't have to pay the 10% additional tax on any part of this distribution. However, they must include the $500 taxable earnings in their gross income subject to income tax." Class A covers $500 in income, no additional tax (Form 5329 line 4 $0). Lines 1 $500, 2 $500 (exception 08) and 3 $0 follow from i5329 p. 5 (line 2, "the amount that you can exclude"); Schedule 2 line 8 $0 and Form 5329 filed (an exception is claimed, i5329 p. 1) follow from the form. Synthetic scaffolding (not in the example): single, wages $50,000 (the stage18.blind.p1 base with its Marketplace coverage removed, and the Form 1099-R entry of stage10.ira.fully_taxable); code 1. The example's $2,700 nontaxable part is a return of nondeductible contributions (basis, Form 8606), which retirement.special refuses; the scaffold therefore enters a $500 distribution with no basis, so Form 1040 line 4a (gross $3,200 in the example) is not asserted. The $5,000 tax-free assistance enters only through the AQEE, entered as the exception 08 amount $800.

Exception 05 is "Qualified retirement plan distributions up to the amount you paid for unreimbursed medical expenses during the year minus 7.5% of your adjusted gross income" (i5329 p. 5, Line 2); with no exception 05 claimed, Form 5329 lines 1 to 4 do not need the medical expenses: line 1 $3,000, line 2 $0, line 3 $3,000, line 4 $300.

Mutation regression (refusal.s2.s2.line8.0), predicted by hand before recording. Blind return E7 (joint; exception 05 claimed for $5,000 by the taxpayer and $3,000 by the spouse) with medical expenses of $15,775. AGI $117,000, 7.5% = $8,775, so Schedule A line 4 is $7,000. i5329 p. 5, Line 2: "up to the amount you paid for unreimbursed medical expenses during the year minus 7.5% of your adjusted gross income (AGI)". Each spouse's amount is within $7,000 (taxpayer line 2 $5,000, line 4 $0; spouse line 2 $3,000, line 4 10% of $4,000 = $400), but together $8,000 exceed it, so Schedule 2 line 8 is refused, and Form 1040 line 23 with it.

s2.line8.remedy: The medical-expense exceptions of both spouses together exceed the medical expenses above 7.5% of your joint AGI; reduce them so that together they do not exceed it.

cite.locator: p. 5, Line 2, "Qualified retirement plan distributions up to the amount you paid for unreimbursed medical expenses during the year minus 7.5% of your adjusted gross income (AGI) for the year."
